blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Holiday Inn Express commercial distribution rides IHG One Rewards direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Midscale limited-service: efficient rooms, Express Start breakfast, and IHG One Rewards distribution for value-conscious transient demand. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus avid's essential midscale positioning, Holiday Inn Express is the scaled midscale limited-service workhorse; versus upscale lifestyle brands, it keeps capital and operating intensity deliberately lean.

blocks.title: Owner Perception Risk
blocks.body: Owners sometimes expect lifestyle lightness without systems cost; Holiday Inn Express still carries parent systems, IHG One Rewards economics, and brand QA. Align IC expectations early.

blocks.title: IHG One Rewards
blocks.body: Holiday Inn Express participates in IHG One Rewards. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: IHG One Rewards at Holiday Inn Express

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn IHG One Rewards points on qualifying stays at Holiday Inn Express. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the IHG One Rewards portfolio, including Holiday Inn Express, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: IHG One Rewards partnerships, co-branded cards, and bonus campaigns expand the loyalty halo; Holiday Inn Express stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: IHG One Rewards drives distribution and repeat demand but adds loyalty chargebacks and program economics. Underwrite net contribution after loyalty—not membership vanity metrics.

blocks.title: P&L Implications
blocks.body: Loyalty assessments and program contribution affect net rooms revenue. Use current agreement exhibits; do not invent undisclosed rates.

blocks.title: Operating Implications
blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support IHG One Rewards enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications
blocks.body: Parent property and reservation systems integration is required for IHG One Rewards participation—budget cutover and training in the conversion plan.

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: IHG One Rewards earn and recognition support repeat Holiday Inn Express stays when the hotel already delivers the brand promise—membership alone does not replace product fit.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: IHG One Rewards member rates and IHG direct paths help Holiday Inn Express defend contribution versus high-commission intermediaries; confirm current rate rules before IC.

blocks.title: Elite Member Value
blocks.body: Elite recognition benefits support contribution at Holiday Inn Express where the property can deliver upgrades and service standards; capability still varies by asset.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: One Rewards recognition across IHG sister brands matters for multi-brand itineraries—Holiday Inn Express is the brand-specific earn/redeem node inside that network.

blocks.title: Partner & Payment Scale
blocks.body: IHG One Rewards partnerships and bonus campaigns expand acquisition; underwrite hotel-level net contribution after loyalty assessments—not headline membership counts.

blocks.title: Corporate & Negotiated Demand
blocks.body: IHG account and negotiated transient patterns can support midweek compression where corporate mix fits Holiday Inn Express—validate against this hotel's source markets.

blocks.title: To Join
blocks.body: Holiday Inn Express application, royalty, program fees, and One Rewards assessments — confirm current IHG disclosure exhibits. Amounts are not staged without a verified disclosure.

blocks.title: To Operate
blocks.body: Steady-state royalty, program contribution, and IHG One Rewards loyalty assessments — confirm definitions, bases, and current percentages in the live disclosure exhibit for Holiday Inn Express. Do not underwrite from peer rumor.

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.title: Fee Variability
blocks.body: Initial vs conversion paths differ; program contribution and loyalty assessments may change by year under agreement terms. Lock the fee exhibit before IC—never extrapolate from a peer hotel's rumor. Geography note: Confirm current IHG development / franchise disclosure for Holiday Inn Express

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add IHG One Rewards: retain Holiday Inn Express's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Midscale limited-service: efficient rooms, Express Start breakfast, and IHG One Rewards distribution for value-conscious transient demand.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.

blocks.title: Corridor Midscale Limited-Service
blocks.body: Highway and suburban corridors where efficient rooms, breakfast, and One Rewards can compete on value.

blocks.title: Airport & Gateway Value
blocks.body: Airport-adjacent value stays where clean product and loyalty distribution matter more than F&B depth.

blocks.title: New-Build Prototype Efficiency
blocks.body: New-build sites optimized for Express prototypes—underwrite development cost discipline against local midscale competitors.

blocks.title: Gateway Urban
blocks.body: Strong Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Holiday Inn Express fits gateway urban demand where parent distribution and loyalty support transient and corporate mixes—underwrite city competitive set.

blocks.title: Conversion & Repositioning
blocks.body: Strong Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Conversion / repositioning is a core owner path when independents seek Holiday Inn Express affiliation and loyalty access—underwrite PIP scope first.

blocks.title: Corporate-Led Urban
blocks.body: Moderate Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Corporate-led urban accounts can pull Holiday Inn Express when the product matches account brand ladders; confirm negotiated rates before assuming contracted volume.

blocks.title: Regional & Secondary Markets
blocks.body: Moderate Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Secondary markets work when Holiday Inn Express's product and fee load clear local ADR reality; diligence source-market seasonality.

blocks.title: Highway & Interstate Transient
blocks.body: Not a Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Highway / interstate limited-service economics generally sit outside Holiday Inn Express's product and fee structure.

blocks.title: Resort & Coastal Leisure
blocks.body: Limited Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Leisure resort fit depends on whether Holiday Inn Express's service model matches resort operating complexity.
